title: Enstrophy Defects and the Stability of Circulating Flows in a Combinatorial Navier–Stokes Model
content: We study Wilson's finite cochain model of incompressible viscous flow on a simplicial 2-complex, in which the velocity is a divergence-free 1-cochain, the pressure a Hodge projection, the viscous term the Hodge Laplacian and the nonlinearity an antisymmetrized cup product. The nonlinearity does no work, but vorticity transport need not conserve enstrophy. The enstrophy production is a weighted sum of local defects over adjacent triangles and vanishes for every 2-cochain exactly when all defects vanish; for closed transporting flows this is a discrete parallelogram rule. Every solution approaches the harmonic cochains, the steady circulations set by the topology, and converges to a single one when the harmonic space is one-dimensional. On diamond-flat complexes, where every harmonic cochain obeys this rule, harmonic flows are normally stable at every amplitude and every solution converges exponentially to one of them. This is sufficient but not necessary: a weighted enstrophy conserved by the linearized transport and dissipated by viscosity gives normal stability at every amplitude on a complex that is not diamond-flat. If the transport operator of a harmonic direction has an eigenvalue off the imaginary axis, the harmonic flows in that direction are Lyapunov unstable above a finite ratio of amplitude to viscosity. On thirty irregular triangulations with one-dimensional harmonic space, the transport operator had such an eigenvalue for both orientations of the generator, the first detected instability was usually oscillatory, and in one case normal stability reappeared on a bounded interval of larger amplitudes.
